story_type: fisherman overboard in near-freezing water, crew pulls him back, litter hoist from a rolling boat
hook: He went overboard into 37 degree water off Alaska.
narration: He went overboard into thirty-seven degree water off Alaska.
He was in the water for twenty-five minutes before the rest of his crew got him back aboard.
This was the fifty-eight foot fishing boat Stella, in Shelikof Strait near Kodiak.
He was hypothermic, so a Coast Guard Jayhawk crew flew out from Air Station Kodiak.
A hypothermic person goes up lying flat in a litter, because rough handling can upset the rhythm of a very cold heart.
[short pause] The hoist operator brought him up over the waves, right to the cabin door.
outcome: The Kodiak aircrew hoisted the crewman off the Stella's deck and into the helicopter.
title: Overboard in 37 degree Alaska water
description:
On March 15, 2013, a Coast Guard Air Station Kodiak MH-60 Jayhawk crew hoisted a hypothermic 35-year-old crewman from the fishing vessel Stella in Shelikof Strait, Alaska, after he spent 25 minutes in 37.6 degree water.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Air Station Kodiak, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/284242/coast-guard-medevacs-crewman-fishing-vessel-near-kodiak-alaska

facts.claim: Kodiak Jayhawk crew hoisted a hypothermic crewman from the 58-foot Stella in Shelikof Strait, March 15, 2013
facts.source_quote: A Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Air Station Kodiak hoists a 35-year-old hypothermic crewman from the deck of the 58-foot Kodiak-based fishing vessel Stella in Shelikof Strait, Alaska, March 15, 2013.

facts.claim: He fell overboard and his crew recovered him after 25 minutes in 37.6 degree water
facts.source_quote: The man fell overboard from the vessel earlier in the day and was recovered from the ocean by the remaining crew after 25 minutes in the 37.6 degree water.
